title: Certificates of Deposit: The Maturity Instruction and Tier Behind a Renewed Term
content:
For the bank's Certificates of Deposit, a renewed term rests on two things recorded on the certificate: the maturity instruction, and the tier the certificate is to continue in. This page states what each must be for a renewal of this kind to exist.

## The instruction on record

A certificate renews only because its record tells it to. A renewal is written only for a certificate whose maturity instruction on record, at the time the renewal is written, is the instruction to renew, and only on a tier that makes renewal without a fresh request available. A certificate whose record carries an instruction to pay out to checking, to pay out to savings, or to mail a check has no renewal written for it; its record points to a different grace outcome.

## The tier the certificate continues in

The pricing described for this renewal covers a certificate that continues in the tier it already holds, that is, a certificate whose tier's renewal tier is its own tier. A certificate whose renewal tier is a different tier is outside it, and no renewal is written under it.

For any renewal, the tier whose published standard figures set the new term's rate is the tier the certificate continues in: its renewal tier when the owner made no change of term during grace, and otherwise the tier the owner chose in grace.

## Input, judgement, outcome (hypothetical certificates; "tier A" and "tier B" stand for any two different tiers)

| Tier held | Instruction on record | That tier's renewal tier | Renewal written here? |
|---|---|---|---|
| tier A | renew | tier A | Yes |
| tier A | renew | tier B | No; the certificate would continue in a different tier |
| tier A | pay out to savings | tier A | No; the record does not instruct renewal |
| tier A | pay out to checking | tier A | No |
| tier A | mail a check | tier A | No |
